title: Practical Lossless Federated Singular Vector Decomposition over Billion-Scale Data

problem.claim: Federated SVD aims to enable SVD-based applications across different data sources without revealing the original data.

gap.claim: Existing federated SVD solutions do not adequately support many SVD-based applications because differential privacy introduces unremovable noise and homomorphic encryption inflates data and reduces efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Privacy-preserving regulations motivate federated SVD for cross-source SVD-based applications without exposing original data.
Many SVD-based applications are not well supported by existing federated SVD solutions.
Existing approaches face an accuracy-efficiency tradeoff: differential privacy causes accuracy loss through unremovable noise, while homomorphic encryption reduces efficiency through data inflation.

source_observation.claim: Existing privacy-preserving federated SVD approaches incur either accuracy loss or efficiency degradation.

interpretation.claim: Privacy mechanisms should be evaluated against both utility and computational efficiency rather than a single performance dimension.

application.claim: When designing federated data-analysis systems, assess whether privacy protection introduces unacceptable noise or data expansion.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this tradeoff applies to every federated SVD implementation or privacy mechanism.

unknowns: The proposed method and its specific algorithmic mechanisms are not described.
No experimental setup, datasets, quantitative results, or billion-scale measurements are supplied.
Privacy guarantees and threat-model details are not supplied.
